lesson_title: 200 Tonnes of Rock for a Kilogram of Gold
hook_text: To get one kilogram of gold, South African miners dig up about 200 tonnes of rock. Here's why.
clip_script: Gold ore in South Africa holds about 5 grams of gold in every tonne of rock. So for 1 kilogram of gold, you dig, crush and process about 200 tonnes. And that rock can be almost four kilometres down, in the deepest mine in the world, where the rock is about 60 degrees and the mine pumps in ice to keep miners cool. If the ore is near the surface, it is cheaper to dig from the top: Sishen's iron ore pit stretches about 14 kilometres. Back in 1871, diggers with shovels made the Big Hole at Kimberley chasing diamonds. And some treasures need no refining at all: diamonds, coal, salt, clay and sand can be used almost straight from the ground.
visual_style: A scale tipping between a mountain of rock and a tiny gold bar; a cage dropping down a shaft; aerial sweep of a giant open pit; sepia photos of the Big Hole.
pacing: Shock-number open, a deep plunge underground, a wide aerial contrast, a quick natural-form roll-call close.
